column1: # conformance/coverage.tsv: every rule of the design's §4.3, §4.6, §4.7, §5.3, §7.1, §7.2, §7.5, §7.6 and §8,
# with what proves it. Columns: ref, rule, cover. A cover token is a case id; `test:<file>::<name>`, a #[test]
# of this crate, for a bound too large for a case; `<owner>:#<issue>` for a part outside this crate (cli,
# server, job, skill); or `git`, git's own behaviour, where no reader acts. tests/coverage.rs checks every token.

column2: rule
Paths are relative to the folder's parent directory and stay inside it; `/`, byte for byte; an entry is a file, a symbolic link or a submodule entry
`*` and `?` stop at `/`; `**` is a whole segment; dot names match; no classes, braces or escapes; a path without `*` or `?` is literal
anchors table, `path`: whether at least one entry matches; a literal path naming a directory holds while a file lies under it
anchors table, `config_key`: the scalar at `<file>#<key path>`, or a list read as layers; or whether the key is present
anchors table, `code`: a literal path plus `text`; whether the text occurs in the file exactly once
a check has exactly one anchor
a glob within one directory merges every matching file; a key in two of them is defined twice; HCL blocks with the same type and labels merge by attribute
layers are read in order; the last layer that defines the key wins; a missing file defines nothing; the key is missing only when no layer defines it
dot segments, quoted segments with `\"` and `\\`, `[n]`, `[k=v]` selectors compared as `==`; a selector that matches nothing is missing, more than one ambiguous
a multi-document file without a root selector holds the key in exactly one document
a key absent from a mapping with a `<<` merge key is `merge key`, never missing
block type, then labels, then nested block types; a repeated nested block is selected like a list element
YAML 1.2 core, JSON, TOML and HCL literals; a file that does not parse is `format`; any other format is unverifiable
a template per value, an HCL expression or `dynamic` block, a Git LFS pointer, a file inside a submodule, a value that is a map or a list
ASCII whitespace removed from both; at least 24 scalar values; at most 2,048 bytes; twice or more is ambiguous; not UTF-8 is `encoding`
exactly one of `must` and `assumes` per check; a check judges whatever the record's kind
`'exist'` or `'<op> <literal>'`, six ops; `exist` holds whatever the value
value table, a number: exact decimal under `==` and `!=`, a literal that is not a decimal is not comparable; ordered ops use the decimal reading only
value table, a string: exact text equality under `==` and `!=`; the readings rule when ordered
value table, a boolean: the literal must be `true` or `false`; ordered is not comparable
value table, `null`: equal only to `null`; ordered is not comparable
decimal and version readings; a number is never a version; a `v` string is a version only; disagreement is `number or version`; a range is unverifiable; SemVer 2.0 precedence
readings table: `'-1'` against `'== -1'` holds: the text is equal
readings table: `'0.8'` against `'< 0.9'` holds: both readings agree
readings table: `'0.9.1'` against `'< 0.9'` is broken: only the version reading applies
readings table: `'3.9'` against `'>= 3.10'` is `number or version`; against `'>= v3.10'` broken
readings table: `'0.5'` against `'<= 0.25'` is `number or version`, never a silent pass
readings table: `2` against `'>= 2'` holds
readings table: `0.5` against `'>= 0.25'` holds: a number is a decimal only
readings table: `true` against `'== yes'` is not comparable: the literal is not a boolean
states table, `holds`: resolved, and the expectation is true
states table, `broken`: a `must` whose expectation is false, or whose file or key is missing
states table, `stale`: an `assumes` whose expectation is false, or whose file or key is missing
states table, `unverifiable`: the reason is always given; a missing file or key is never unverifiable; never reported as holds
`invalid`, else `superseded`, else the worst of its checks; a record without checks holds
`.knowledge/` at the root and in any subdirectory; records are the `*.md` files anywhere under `<folder>/records/`
`.knowledge/README.md` exists only at the root
discovery reads the path set of H, never the disk; `record` stages the file it writes
`applies_to` defaults to the files the record's checks anchor
a record covering its whole folder is context for every file there; `status` names every such record
every record from every folder on each path's way up whose `applies_to` matches, read from front matter only
superseded and invalid records never route; `status` lists them
`broken` and `stale` first, the nearest folder, the narrowest glob, a `must` first, kind, title, id
the cap of 20 after ordering, then `N more (K broken or stale)`
an unknown check kind or op is `unverifiable: unknown`; the record still routes and shows
a newer schema's checks are `unverifiable: newer schema`, title and kind shown, never rewritten; a `knowledge` that is not an integer is invalid
`x-` keys are ignored silently; other unknown keys are reported once
the corpus carries unknown keys, check kinds and ops, and a newer schema that supersedes a schema-1 record
H is `<rev>`'s tree, else the tree `git add -u` then `git write-tree` would write, computed without changing the index
B is the tree of the merge base of `<base>` and H's commit; several merge bases exit 3
both trees are read by exact byte path from git's objects; a partial clone fetches what it needs; a shallow clone without B exits 3
a check is live when its record is valid, of schema 1 and not superseded
same id, verb, parsed expectation and key path or text; each path equal or following
the same check is sought only among records in folders above a changed path (Q5)
a live `must` of H `broken` at H unless the same check was live and `broken` in B; or `unverifiable` at H after holding at B
a live `must` of B not `broken` at B, with no same check live in H, `broken` at H as B wrote it, or `unverifiable` after holding
a live `must` of B with no same check in H that rule 2 does not break; the finding says what happened
a live `assumes` of H that does not hold at H, unless it did not hold at B; the note names a same-content file
a check rule 1 excused: one count line, never a finding
records added, edited or removed; anchors that followed a moved file; a new `must` that is `unverifiable` at H
a duplicate id it adds; a `supersedes` it writes naming another folder's record, an unknown id or its own record
a check that was never verifiable; a record the change did not touch
one finding per record and anchored key; the worst class wins; every reason listed
a record never excuses its own change; a decision turned into a question keeps its checks
a constraint comes down in a change of its own (Q2)
a moved file takes its anchor along in the same change; left behind, it is `broken` naming the same-content file
a constraint that comes back judges at once
unknown is not an excuse: rule 1 excuses only a check `broken` at B
a new check that cannot be judged is listed under knowledge changes; `record` refuses it
a check none of whose inputs changed keeps its state; only folders above changed paths are read; `--no-renames`
text with at most 10 findings, then `N more`; `--json` (`format: 1`); `--sarif` (SARIF 2.1.0)
0; 2 under `--fail-on broken`; a pathspec after `--`; 3 on usage, a missing object, several merge bases or a base not in local history; a bound is never an exit code
the job judges a merge commit against its first parent, `docbrain status --base M^1 M`; fetch depth 2
`pull_request_target`, read-only, the CLI pinned by version and checksum, the change read only as objects; elsewhere `CODEOWNERS` or protected configuration
the CLI's text printed between stop-commands tokens; annotation messages escaped
blocking is sound only on an up-to-date target; the scheduled `status --fail-on broken` reports the rest
text and the exit code by default; SARIF upload optional; the judging records come from the target
every output frames records as data with a per-call delimiter and indented or escaped bodies
the set named against Unicode 17.0: C0 and C1 controls, format characters, variation selectors; a BOM at the start, joiners between letters and the three direction marks allowed
`record` refuses to write a hidden-text character
records proposed in the change are labelled not reviewed; in CI the judging records come from the merge base and the target's job file
the server indexes only the default branch
the skill, the README and the pointer say records are facts, not instructions
relative to the folder's parent and inside it; no `..` segment, leading `/`, drive letter, `~` or backslash; never under `.git/`
a symbolic link is a tree entry of mode 120000, never followed: an anchor naming one or through one is `symbolic link`; a record file that is one is invalid
writes from `record` obey the same rule
an exceeded bound is `unverifiable` (or an `invalid` record) with the bound named; a `must` that held at B and crosses a bound at H is `broken`
64 KiB, checked from the tree entry's size before reading
8 KiB, nesting depth 32
per format, well above the largest real files of that format, lockfiles included
64; alias expansion in anchored YAML capped
100,000; the excess, in byte order of path, listed in one line by folder
p95 under 300 ms per edit; at most 20 records and 4 KiB per edit
a duplicate key on an anchored path is `defined twice`
a scalar YAML 1.1 and 1.2 read differently is unverifiable whatever the expectation; `on:` is a string key
a merge key a key may come from makes an absent key `merge key`
a change that moves a guarded value into such a shape is `broken`, not silence
two branches create records concurrently: different ids, different files, no conflict
two branches edit one record: conflict markers make it invalid until resolved
one branch removes a record, another edits it: the person merging decides
a record file renamed or moved into a subdirectory: identity is the id; the name is cosmetic
squash merges and rebases: identity by id; sync is idempotent
an anchored file moved with its anchor in the same change: the same check at the new path
an anchored file moved, the anchor left behind: `broken` with "update the anchor", or `stale`
a whole directory moves with its folder and records: every anchor follows
a file moves out of its folder's parent: the record moves with it, or it is broken
a record moved to another folder with its anchors rewritten: the same check
code moved from a file that remains: not the same check
a guarded key restructured in its file: `broken`; a key path changed in the same change
a record deleted: rule 2 judges its `must` checks at H
a service decommissioned in one change is `broken`; in two changes `changed`, then nothing
removing a body for privacy: the next sync drops it
`supersedes` naming an unknown id, another folder's record or its own: a finding, no effect
a supersession cycle: a finding; no member is superseded
a change supersedes a `must` and breaks it: rule 2
the superseding record deleted, or a record repaired from invalid: rule 1 with no excuse
two records with one id in one folder: both evaluate; a finding on the change; the server indexes the first
`knowledge: 2` is `newer schema`, never rewritten; `1.0` or `'1'` is invalid
a record changed to `knowledge: 2`: rule 2 judges B's checks
a schema-2 record that supersedes a schema-1 record: honoured
an unknown key is reported once; an `x-` key is ignored
anchors, aliases, tags, merge keys or duplicate keys in front matter: invalid
a plain or double-quoted string in front matter: `use single quotes`; `knowledge: 1` the one integer
a body above 64 KiB is refused; the context output shows the first paragraph and the path
an empty body: `record` refuses; a hand-written one is invalid
a binary or non-`.md` file under `records/`: ignored, reported once
an id starting `0000` is invalid
a hidden-text character, an ANSI escape or a run of variation selectors: invalid with line and column
a body in any language with the three direction marks is valid; bidirectional controls stay invalid
CRLF or a BOM accepted on read; the CLI writes LF without a BOM
two slugs that differ only by case: two ids, two files
an agent writes 500 records in one change: listed under knowledge changes; no cap
an agent pins a value it just chose under `must`: listed for review; the skill's eval suite catches it
a record about another repository's path: no cross-repository anchor in schema 1
a leading `/`, `..`, a drive letter, `~`, a backslash, or under `.git/`: invalid; on Windows `record` writes `/`
a symbolic link as an anchored file or a component: `symbolic link`; as a record file: invalid
`app/[slug]/page.tsx` is literal
`docs/**` is every file under `docs/`, never a file named `docs`
a directory path under `exist` holds while a file lies under it
an anchor on an ignored or untracked file: not in H, so `broken` or `stale`; the reason "not tracked"; `record` refuses it
an anchor inside a git submodule: `inside a submodule`
an anchored file stored in Git LFS: `LFS pointer`; `record` refuses it
a root record and a nested record both match: both shown, nearest first
`applies_to` matching nothing: context for nothing; `status` says so
the guarded line deleted, or the key missing: `broken` under `must`, `stale` under `assumes`
a guarded value replaced by an expression, a template or a range: rule 1, no longer checkable
`unverifiable` at B then violated at H is `broken`; unverifiable at both is never a finding
a new `must` that is `unverifiable` at H: listed under knowledge changes; `record` refuses it
a layer whose file is missing defines nothing
`terraform {}` in two files merges by attribute; an attribute set twice is `defined twice`
a key absent beside a `<<` merge key: `merge key`
a multi-document YAML file with the key in two documents: `ambiguous`
an Ansible vars file with one Jinja value: that value is `template`; the other keys resolve
`on:` is a string key; `on`, `off`, `yes`, `no`, `y`, `n`, `0755`, `1:30` are unverifiable
TOML datetimes are text under `==`, not comparable when ordered; `.inf`, `.nan` not comparable; `0x1F` is 31
a selector value is compared as `==` compares
an ordered comparison between a version and a non-version: not comparable
a decimal string whose two readings disagree: `number or version`; `record` refuses it
a `code` file not UTF-8: `encoding`; only ASCII whitespace removed; the floor counts scalar values
a formatter re-wraps or re-indents guarded code: holds
the guarded text left in a comment: holds
an anchored file grows past its bound: `unverifiable` with the bound; held at B, so `broken`
a change edits a `must` so the new one passes while the old one is violated: rule 2
a change only removes, loosens or supersedes a `must`: `changed`; the next change may alter the value
a tightened `must`: `changed: expectation`; the new check judged by rule 1
a decision turned into a question: the kind never changes judging
a dependency bump that trips an `assumes`: `stale`; one that trips a `must`: `broken`
a shallow CI clone without the base commit: exit 3 with the fetch hint
several merge bases: exit 3, "pass the base commit"; the reference job passes `M^1`
a pull request into a release branch, or a retargeted stacked one: merge commit against its first parent
two changes that pass alone and break together: caught only with up-to-date branches or a merge queue, else by the scheduled status
a change edits the job file or its flags: `pull_request_target`, or `CODEOWNERS` and protected configuration
a proposed record with a workflow-command line: printed between stop-commands tokens
`diff.renames`, `diff.renameLimit` or `merge.renames` set locally: no effect
a sparse checkout or sparse index: H takes paths outside the cone from the index; anchors read from objects
a blobless partial clone: one batch of fetches; offline with a missing object, exit 3
context for 5,000 paths: routing through the cache, then the cap
more than 100,000 records: the excess, in byte order of path, listed in one line by folder
more than 1,000 files in one directory under `records/`: the README suggests one per year
a subagent edits a file its parent already saw records for: the hook's dedupe is keyed by the receiving context
offline, air-gapped or the server down: everything local works; sync resumes
records on a non-default branch: local tools read H; the server reads the default branch only
the folder inside a Docker context, a Helm package or an npm package: the README gives the ignore lines
root records filling every edit's context: local and narrow first, the cap announced; `status` names every folder-wide record
